snug — what this sandbox would be. Nothing was started.

The project directory, writable from inside:
  /home/u/proj/sub
Your home directory:
  /home/u
Both keep the exact path they have on your host. snug never relocates a path,
because a tool that prints an absolute path inside should print one that means
the same thing outside.

Selected profiles:
  @sys @home @cwd-rw @net
A profile only ever GRANTS. There is no rule anywhere that takes something
away, so adding a profile can only ever make the sandbox see more, and the way
to see less is to select fewer.

FILESYSTEM
  The root is an empty tmpfs. It has 11 paths read-only, 9 writable, and
  4 files snug generates itself rather than binding from your host.
  Everything else on this machine is not missing by a rule — it was never
  granted, so there is nothing there to deny.

  Writable, which is the half worth reading twice:
    /dev
    /home/u
    /home/u/.cache
    /home/u/.config
    /home/u/.local/share
    /home/u/.local/state
    /home/u/proj/sub
    /proc
    /tmp

WHAT IS NOT IN HERE
  No X11 and no Wayland: a GUI program will not open a window, and nothing
  inside can read your screen or your keystrokes.
  No D-Bus, session or system. No host abstract sockets of any kind.
  No host loopback. A service you are running on 127.0.0.1 is unreachable
  from inside, under every profile, including the networked ones.
  No ~/.ssh. Your private keys are not in this filesystem at all.
  No root, no setuid, and no process snug did not start — everything here
  dies with the sandbox.

NETWORK
  Full outbound internet, through a pasta helper in a namespace of its own.
  Host loopback stays unreachable — pasta is started with -T none, so a
  port on your own machine is not a port from in here.
  DNS: none — a profile asked for it and this host names no usable
  resolver, so lookups inside will fail immediately rather than stall.

COMMAND
  /bin/sh

This is the summary. `snug --dry-run` has the complete list — every mount, every
environment variable, the bwrap argv — and is the screen to read when you are
checking snug rather than orienting yourself.
